acceptance_criteria.criterion: parseGitCredentials() correctly migrates an old Record<string, string> config to GitCredentialEntry[], preserving all host-token pairs.
Migrated entries have id derived from the hostname in kebab-case, label set to the hostname value.
Migration is idempotent — re-parsing an already-migrated array produces the same result.
parseGitCredentials() rejects arrays with duplicate id values.
parseGitCredentials() rejects entries with empty id, label, host, or token fields.
When two old-format entries would produce the same kebab-case ID, a numeric suffix is appended to disambiguate.
All unit tests in src/tests/config.test.ts for migration and validation pass.

comments.note: A09 / Information Disclosure — src/config/config.ts:235-238: The legacy-format error message for an invalid token type exposes the hostname key in the error string: `gitCredentials["${host}"] must be a string, got ${typeof token}`. If application error output is captured in shared or forwarded logs, this leaks hostnames that have associated credentials. Recommendation: mask or omit the hostname in the error message, e.g. use `gitCredentials[entry #${index}]` instead of interpolating the raw key.

A04 / Insecure Design — src/config/config.ts (parseGitCredentials, new-format array path): No maximum length validation is applied to the `token`, `id`, `label`, or `host` fields. An adversarially crafted config.json with extremely long strings could cause memory pressure at load time. Low risk for a local developer tool, but a simple guard (e.g. reject fields exceeding 4096 chars) would add defence-in-depth.

A04 / Insecure Design — src/config/config.ts (parseGitCredentials, both paths): The `host` field is accepted as any non-empty string without hostname format validation. A malformed value (e.g. containing path traversal sequences, null bytes, or whitespace) could cause unexpected behaviour in downstream git credential matching (WP-005/WP-007 scope). Recommendation: validate `host` against a basic hostname pattern (e.g. no slashes, no null bytes, must resemble a domain or IP) in a future WP.

A02 / Cryptographic Failures (defence-in-depth) — src/config/config.ts:300-302: saveConfigField() correctly applies chmodSync(0o600) after writing config.json on POSIX systems to restrict token file to owner-only read/write. This is a positive security control. Note: on Windows, no equivalent permission restriction is applied — acceptable for a local tool but worth documenting in the README.

No hardcoded secrets, test tokens, or credential values found in config.dist.json or any test fixtures. config.dist.json uses an empty array [] for gitCredentials — no sample/placeholder token values that could be mistakenly committed.

comments.note: Maintainability — parseGitCredentials() is very well decomposed. The two branches (array path vs. legacy-object path) are clearly separated with inline comments, and the JSDoc is accurate and complete. The use of `as const` on the field array ['id','label','host','token'] is a nice touch that gives TypeScript a literal tuple and keeps the loop type-safe. No unnecessary complexity observed.

Best Practices — The type assertion pattern `entry = value[i] as Record<string, unknown>` followed immediately by a runtime `typeof entry !== 'object'` guard is idiomatic TypeScript for parsing unknown JSON. The assertion widens to a working type while the runtime guard provides safety. This is the correct pattern for this context — no use of any unsafe `any`-based shortcuts. Consistent with how other parsers in the codebase handle raw config fields.

Best Practices — ID deduplication logic (lines 188/231, `Set<string>`) is correct and efficient. The loop appends a numeric suffix starting at 2 — the convention is intuitive (matches common OS file-copy conventions like 'file (2)'). One observation: the suffix counter is not reset between entries, which is correct behavior. No bug here.

Performance — No performance concerns in the new-format validation path. The O(n) loop over entries with a Set for duplicate detection is optimal. The legacy-format migration uses Object.entries() which is O(n) — equally appropriate. No redundant passes over the array. Config parsing is startup-time only, so even a quadratic approach would be acceptable for realistic credential counts, but the O(n) approach is clean.

Future Context — The dual-format parser (new array + legacy object) is a well-designed migration bridge. Having the migration logic colocated with validation (rather than in a separate migration module) is appropriate given the scope — it keeps the parsing contract self-contained. As credential management grows (WP-005, WP-007), the decision to use GitCredentialEntry[] with a stable `id` field as the lookup key gives downstream consumers a clean reference contract.

Future Context — The _defaultsCoverageGuard pattern (lines 37-42) is an excellent compile-time completeness guard. Any future AppConfig field addition will surface at this line if DEFAULTS is not updated. This is a proactive maintainability investment and worthy of being documented as a project convention.

Hostname leak in legacy error messages (Security Auditor Medium finding, lines 236 and 241): The messages `gitCredentials["${host}"] must be a string` and `gitCredentials["${host}"] must not be an empty string` embed the raw hostname into the error string. Fix-Forward was considered but not applied: the existing test at config.test.ts:379 asserts on the regex /gitCredentials\["github\.com"\].*string/, which would fail if the message format changes. This requires a coordinated Developer fix + test update. Recommend replacing `"${host}"` with a positional reference (e.g. `entry #${index}`) in both throw messages and updating the two corresponding test assertions to match the new format.

[documentation-forward] The _defaultsCoverageGuard pattern in src/config/config.ts (lines 37-42) is a valuable compile-time completeness guard. Add a comment in the config/README.md or inline at the declaration site explaining the pattern's intent — specifically that any new AppConfig field without a default will surface as a type error here, preventing silent omissions at runtime.

[documentation-forward] The {} empty object vs [] empty array asymmetry in parseGitCredentials() (undefined vs [] return value) is documented in JSDoc but not in config/README.md or any user-facing config guide. The next documentation pass should add a note explaining: 'omit gitCredentials or leave as null/{}  → treated as no credentials (undefined); use [] to explicitly set an empty credential list.' This distinction matters for consumers checking `config.gitCredentials !== undefined`.
